description.narrative: The development objective of Sustainable Management of Substances Controlled by the Montreal Protocol Project is to reduce HFC and HCFC consumption in support of Viet Nam's obligations under the Montreal Protocol. This project has three components. The first component, HFC Consumption Reductions, has the following sub-components: Developing and testing refrigerant technology to reduce high-GWP HFCs in MAC train systems; Reducing HFC consumption and emissions in MAC repair and maintenance through provision of: (a) training equipment to the MAC sector training and/or assessment centers, and (b) MAC servicing tools to technicians as incentive for participating in training and/or completing assessment for certification; and Supporting: (a) awareness raising activities, training, and study tours on lower-GWP alternative technology for priority sectors, including real estate, fire suppression, and rail; (b) research and development of guidance and related management measures on reducing HFCs in relevant sectors, including domestic and stand-alone commercial refrigeration, fire suppression, train and bus MAC, and AC using high GWP HFCs; and (c) feasibility studies on HFC phasedown and management in public transport, non-HFC alternatives in fire suppression, and green public procurement of lower-GWP products. The second component, HCFC Consumption Reductions, has the following sub-components: Strengthening AC servicing sector training capacity through (a) training of trainers at the AC sector training centers on AC good servicing and energy efficiency maintenance practices, (b) provision of training equipment to the AC training centers, and (c) training AC servicing technicians; Strengthening competency-based servicing capacity in the AC servicing sector through (a) development of a vocational skills competency-based certification scheme for AC, (b) training of assessors, (c) provision of assessment equipment to AC sector assessment centers, and (d) provision of AC servicing tools to technicians as incentive for participating in training and/or completing assessment for certification; and Providing technical assistance and capacity building support for sustainable HCFC phaseout. The third component, Project Management, will be established and operated within DCC.
The project development objective is to increase formal private sector employment among targeted groups of registered jobseekers.
